A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoAuteur and CookGen. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original caption-quality evaluations, latent-space and regression experiments, human ratings, and video-generation results in Sections 3.3 and 5, with supplementary examples and analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds rolling-context renderer evaluations, external-method comparisons, and regularization ablations in Section 5.

M1.justification: V2 adds a rolling-context keyframe renderer between the interleaved director and video generator. This FLUX.1 Fill-based component combines tiled captions, predicted visual embeddings, and reference-image VAE features, using a flow-matching objective (Section 4.2). It substantially changes keyframe synthesis; the existing director and noise-regularization operators are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CookGen cooking data sourced from YouCook2 and HowTo100M, covering caption assessment, inverse reconstruction, narrative keyframes, and video generation. The additional renderer and baseline experiments remain within this established coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 adds evaluated comparisons with IC Lora, StoryDiffusion, Vlogger, and SEED-Story, alongside retained SD-XL and FLUX.1-s. V1 Table 8's SEED-X results reappear as the method without rolling-context conditioning. EMU-2 disappears from that human comparison, although its latent-space comparison remains in Appendix F.

E3.justification: The existing splits, preprocessing, and director/video-model training budgets remain unchanged. The expanded keyframe comparison adds CLIP-T/FID reporting, specifies two-epoch adaptation for IC Lora and SEED-Story, and marks SD-XL/FLUX narrative ratings as inapplicable. The new renderer introduces a four-image, 5,000-step training configuration; these are additions within the retained evaluation framework.

E4.justification: V2 adds a with/without rolling-context comparison in Table 4 and explicit regularization controls in Tables 3 and 7, including cumulative masking, Gaussian noise, and shuffling. Conversely, the EMU-2 portion of v1's loss ablation is removed. The latent-space comparison and perturbation visualizations are retained in Appendix F, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The six caption-evaluation annotators are documented in both. V2's Gaussian-noise standard deviation specifies perturbation strength, not uncertainty in reported performance.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial baseline and renderer results. Table 4 reports CLIP-T/FID of 28.0/29.4 with rolling context, versus retained values of 26.1/25.3 without it; corresponding aesthetics, realism, consistency, and narrative ratings are 4.8/4.5/4.8/4.6 versus 2.1/4.3/4.5/4.4. Regularization intermediate results are added, while EMU-2 loss/human results and SD-XL/FLUX narrative scores are dropped. Matched final video-generation and caption-quality scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 Section 4.2 adds mathematical definitions for tiled captions, joint keyframe conditioning, and the renderer's flow-matching objective in Equations 5–7. The earlier autoregressive factorization, regression loss, and regularization mathematics remain. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V1 presents a two-component pipeline and emphasizes empirical exploration of interleaved generation. V2 redefines the contribution around integrating multimodal autoregression with a rolling-context DiT renderer and explicitly claims state-of-the-art narrative-generation performance in the introduction. The CookGen contribution and abstract are largely retained.

C2.justification: V1 accepts an aesthetics-versus-consistency tradeoff and argues that consistency deserves priority. V2 instead explains how reference-image VAE features preserve detail while CLIP conditioning preserves semantics, and discusses a context-length efficiency/consistency tradeoff and baseline-specific visual failures. The existing ASR-noise, repeated-step, and hallucination limitations remain in Appendix H.

D1.justification: V2 identifies FLUX.1 Fill initialization and supplies the new renderer's full configuration in Appendix D, including AdamW settings, learning rate, batch size, training steps, and masking probability. It also newly specifies the existing regularization's masking/shuffling rates and noise scale estimated from 2,000 embeddings. V1's explicit director LoRA and Sora-like video-model descriptions are dropped; the project-page access information is retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds IC Lora, CLIPScore, and FID references and removes the LLM-grounded video diffusion reference. The narrative-generation discussion shifts from emphasizing proximity to SEED-Story toward positioning the method as an integrated multimodal-LLM/in-context-DiT approach. Most related work remains, including the FLUX work under revised bibliographic wording.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially condensed and rewritten, the method hierarchy is reorganized around three components, and the experiments gain separate comparison and ablation sections. Dataset-quality evaluation moves from Section 3.3 into Appendix C, while much of the latent-space analysis moves into Appendix F. This is extensive narrative restructuring despite substantial retained text.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 3 to include the renderer, expands Figure 4 with regularization illustrations, adds rolling-context examples and an annotation-evaluation diagram, and replaces the main qualitative comparison. The principal comparison table gains methods, metrics, and prompting columns; the loss table loses its EMU-2 block. Several retained displays move to the appendices, whose implementation and algorithm layouts also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical case beyond v1's mostly internal comparisons: relevant narrative baselines and explicit renderer and regularization controls address important gaps in comparative and component-level evidence (Tables 3, 4, and 7). Appendix D also documents the new renderer's training. There are material qualifications: rolling context worsens FID from 25.3 to 29.4, the prose combines best CLIP-T and FID scores from different variants, and some EMU-2 evidence is removed. These issues weaken blanket superiority claims, but the added comparative and controlled evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
